tasks.short: Assess live traffic and issue landing or take-off instructions

steps.what: Assess aircraft, runway conditions and traffic before selecting landing or take-off instructions
Issue the checked instructions by radio and resolve pilot readback discrepancies

tasks.design: Retain live assessment and clearance communication with the controller using the {OTHER} air traffic surveillance, electronic strip and radio systems. Existing displays support the decision, while the controller checks current conditions, issues the instruction and resolves readback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clearance depends on rapidly changing physical conditions and coordinated aircraft intentions.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic records can support situational awareness, but the supplied evidence does not establish a new labour-saving clearance design.
tasks.still_hard: A clearance that was appropriate moments ago may become unsafe before transmission.
tasks.human_edge: The controller integrates incomplete observations and immediately corrects misunderstandings.
tasks.altitude: No change to decision rights, workload or responsibility is claimed.

reach.task: Read back and act on a clearance
reach.learn: How ambiguous or blocked transmissions affect crew understanding

evidence.claim: Frequentis smartSTRIPS replaced paper strips in two Schiphol towers in 2019; this supports electronic strip availability, not autonomous clearance or a saving in this task.
Retaining controller assessment, transmission and readback resolution is a model-knowledge design boundary.

assumptions: Boundary starts with live assessment for a requested movement and ends with communicated clearance and resolved readback; aircraft operation and ongoing surveillance outside that episode are separate.

Existing surveillance services produce aircraft identity, position, altitude and timestamps; airfield staff provide runway status and pilots communicate requests. These are existing inputs, not free newly structured eligibility flags.

Controller interpretation, confirmation of missing or conflicting information and readback handling remain fully counted in s1 and s2. No automatic clearance calculation is proposed; degraded information uses existing manual operating procedures.
Test native display and strip capabilities before considering any separate project. OTHER denotes air traffic surveillance, electronic strips and radio communication systems.
Zero incremental upkeep is justified because no new automation, integration or record is introduced; existing system maintenance remains outside the change.
unknowns: How current runway status reaches the controller
research_questions: Which observed delays arise from display access rather than the required live clearance conversation?

already_counted.description: Live assessment, clearance checking and readback resolution

incremental.description: No new process or system upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact aircraft, runway, instruction and current traffic context checked immediately before each transmission in s2; any changed condition voids it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net are zero with zero incremental upkeep. Existing electronic strips do not remove live assessment, transmission or readback time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check conditions and traffic for requested altitude changes

steps.what: Check conditions and traffic at requested altitudes using surveillance, weather and pilot information

tasks.design: Keep the controller's altitude assessment within the {OTHER} air traffic surveillance and flight information environment. Existing tools show traffic and weather, while the controller checks relevance, uncertainty and coordination before any separate clearance action.
tasks.previous_blocker: An altitude request cannot be assessed from a static list without interpreting the changing traffic situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Current displays already assist this check; the supplied digest gives no task-specific evidence that a new tool reduces the controller's assessment time.
tasks.still_hard: Weather, aircraft performance and adjacent traffic intentions may be incomplete or change during assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The controller weighs conflicting observations and identifies when more coordination is needed.
tasks.altitude: The controller retains the same assessment duties and authority.

reach.task: Explain operational reasons for a requested altitude change
reach.learn: How turbulence and aircraft limitations affect the request

evidence.claim: Keeping live altitude suitability assessment with the controller is a model-knowledge boundary; no measured saving is inferred from flight planning or electronic strip products.

assumptions: Boundary is checking the requested altitude, ending before issuing a clearance or executing the aircraft movement.

Pilots provide requested altitude and operational reasons; existing surveillance and meteorological services produce identity, position, altitude, observation time and weather information. No newly captured suitability code is presumed.
All interpretation, checking timestamps, resolving missing information and manual coordination remain in s1 at full time. Existing degraded-mode procedures apply when feeds are unavailable.
Test the native capabilities of the approved environment before proposing custom code. OTHER denotes air traffic surveillance and flight information systems.
Zero incremental upkeep reflects an unchanged workflow and no new data capture or automation.
unknowns: Division of coordination duties across sectors
research_questions: Does observation show any repeated retrieval activity separable from the required altitude assessment?

already_counted.description: Interpret live conditions and resolve uncertain altitude information

incremental.description: No additional upkeep for an unchanged assessment process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and focal incremental=0. No saving is claimed from already-running surveillance or weather feeds; all assessment and coordination remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Initiate and coordinate searches for missing aircraft

steps.what: Verify missing aircraft information and establish last contact, location uncertainty and reporting context
Initiate searches and coordinate changing information with the responsible rescue and control teams

tasks.design: Use the existing {OTHER} air traffic records and emergency communication systems to establish incident information and coordinate the search. Retain controller verification, escalation and live exchanges with rescue teams; no search initiation is delegated to a model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searches start with incomplete, conflicting and time-sensitive information rather than a reliable missing-aircraft flag.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records help reconstruct last contact, but the digest offers no demonstrated replacement for this emergency coordination.
tasks.still_hard: The controller must distinguish missing information from evidence of an emergency and update others as facts change.
tasks.human_edge: The controller makes accountable escalation decisions and communicates uncertainty precisely.
tasks.altitude: Emergency responsibilities and required coordination time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Support search coordination with local aircraft and airfield information
reach.learn: Incident information handover and uncertainty reporting

evidence.claim: Retaining verified incident assessment and human search coordination is a model-knowledge design, without a measured labour-saving case in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary covers controller verification and search initiation or coordination, not rescue-team deployment labour or the physical search.

Existing flight and communication services supply identity, flight plan, last recorded position, timestamp and contact history; callers provide the initial concern. The controller checks provenance and uncertainty in fully counted s1.

Rescue teams produce subsequent search updates during s2 exchanges; those updates are not assumed available before coordination begins. Missing records trigger manual enquiries under existing procedures, all retained in s1 or s2.
Test existing emergency communication and record functions before custom code. OTHER denotes air traffic records and emergency communication systems.
Zero added upkeep is justified because this design introduces no new system, structured flag or reporting obligation.
research_questions: Which incident information is unavailable during exercises, and who must provide it?

already_counted.description: Incident verification, escalation checking and live search coordination

incremental.description: No new automation or additional record maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact incident facts, uncertainty, intended escalation and recipient checked immediately before each s2 communication; updates require fresh checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross zero minus zero upkeep gives net zero. Verifying a missing-aircraft concern and coordinating evolving search information retain their full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide on-the-job training to new controllers

steps.what: Provide supervised on-the-job training, observe controller performance, intervene and discuss decisions

tasks.design: Retain direct supervision and feedback while the trainee uses the {OTHER} air traffic control workstation. The instructor observes decisions and intervenes when required; no reduction in supervision is inferred from electronic records.
tasks.previous_blocker: On-the-job training depends on observing attention, timing and judgement during real operations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workstations support shared observation, but the digest gives no evidence that a new tool replaces instructor supervision.
tasks.still_hard: A correct outcome alone does not reveal whether the trainee understood the situation or was merely fortunate.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor identifies reasoning weaknesses and adapts coaching while preserving operational control.
tasks.altitude: Training responsibility, supervision time and certification rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Communicate clearly with controllers during demanding situations
reach.learn: Crew workload and the operational effect of instruction timing

evidence.claim: Live instructor observation, intervention and feedback are a model-knowledge boundary for on-the-job controller training; no task-specific saving is documented in this digest.

assumptions: Boundary covers the instructor's direct on-the-job coaching, not classroom material preparation, separate certification decisions or the trainee's own labour.

Training staff provide objectives and the trainee produces observable actions during practice. The instructor interprets those actions directly; no structured competence flag or automatic assessment is presumed.
Observation, clarification, intervention and feedback remain fully counted in s1. Missing information is explored in conversation and existing training procedures, without machine inference.
Test native training support before considering separate software. OTHER denotes the existing air traffic control workstation.
No additional tooling or record capture is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; existing training administration is outside this task boundary.
unknowns: Instructor qualification and local supervision requirements
research_questions: Which reasoning difficulties become visible only during instructor debriefing?

incremental.description: No new training-support system or capture work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental=0. Required supervision and adaptive feedback remain unchanged; no clerical preparation baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Live control, emergency coordination and instructor responsibility remain with qualified controllers, with no claimed labour reduction for these tasks.
reach: Practise precise emergency handovers with airfield teams
